scope: WP10 finite GitHub compensating commit for exact succeeded forward commits
implemented: Rollback is absent by default and requires grant.rollback with allowRollback true plus a dedicated Policy budget ID, maximum action count and maximum byte count.

At compensation time (never before dispatch), the Host reads each exact grant-scoped path at the immutable parent commit identified by the forward receipt's expectedHeadOid; only canonical bounded UTF-8 files or exact 404 absence are accepted.

A path 404 is not trusted by itself: the same immutable parent commit is read through the Git Data API (git/commits/{oid} then git/trees/{tree_sha}?recursive=1) and its blob index must corroborate every result. A 404 for a path the immutable tree lists as a blob, a contents blob OID that disagrees with the tree, an unexpected commit/tree OID, a truncated or oversized tree, or any index fetch failure fails closed: capture aborts and no compensation commit is sent. This prevents a fine-grained PAT lacking Contents read (branches 200, contents 404) or a >100 MiB blob (contents 404) from turning live files into deletions.

The complete present/absent preimage and digest stay in the private ledger; the model-visible succeeded forward result exposes only forwardActionId, forwardActionVersion, forwardRequestDigest and forwardCommitOid.
A compensation request references the exact redacted forward receipt and does not accept paths, files, content or preimage from the caller.
Owner, Session, grant revision, repository, branch, paths, forward action/version/request digest/commit OID, private preimage and current rollback authority are rebound before dispatch.
Each exact succeeded forward action has at most one compensation record; alternate idempotency keys cannot create another attempt.

Compensation first requires the branch head to equal the forward commit and then sends one ordinary createCommitOnBranch mutation with that expected head, restoring prior files and deleting paths that were previously absent.
The protocol never force-pushes, resets, calls updateRef or rewrites history; later branch changes produce a conflict.

A dispatched compensation is sent once. Timeout, cancellation, redirect, lost acknowledgement or malformed/mismatched response remains unknown and is not replayed after restart; on restart, prepared/dispatched rows are recovered to unknown (never re-dispatched) while capturing placeholder rows that never sealed a preimage are deleted, freeing the forward action's one-compensation slot and its action budget.

Before dispatch, a denied second-stage budget authorization, an expired authority or a fail-closed capture error discards the capturing placeholder so a pre-dispatch failure can neither wedge the forward action nor permanently consume a rollback action; once the preimage is sealed but the local dispatch flip has not happened, an authorization/hold failure terminalizes the prepared row to unknown live (reason authorization-ended-before-dispatch, audited compensation-abandoned) instead of leaving a zombie 'prepared' that only the next process restart would clear.

A GraphQL rejection (errors entry, CAS conflict, or mismatched commit/parent/ref in the mutation response) settles the compensation as failed with reason github-compensation-rejected and is never retried or misreported as succeeded.
File compensation does not retract pull requests, CI, reviews, comments, messages, notifications, webhooks, deployments, releases or other external side effects.

independentSecurityReview.summary: An independent adversarial reviewer read the frozen WP10 diff against base cb46b2d in a read-only pass (no network, no git writes) and concluded the change is safe to merge to dev in its default-off configuration. No CRITICAL or HIGH findings. All ten safety invariants were CONFIRMED against source. Four LOW followups and seven test gaps were recorded; all four LOW items were dispositioned in followup (LOW-1/LOW-2 closed with code+tests, LOW-3/LOW-4 retained as intentional conservative boundaries), and every recorded test gap except the v2-to-v3 ledger migration coverage is now closed (see testGapDisposition and secondPassReview).

lowFollowups.issue: The tree index records only blob entries, so a 404 for a submodule (type=commit) or directory (type=tree) path lacks the same cross-validation as a blob path.
lowFollowups.exploitability: Not exploitable on real GitHub: both kinds return 200 from contents, and deleting them is rejected by mutation errors. Hardening only.
lowFollowups.recommendation: Record non-blob tree entry types and fail closed when a 404 matches any indexed entry.
lowFollowups.evidence: github.ts readGitHubTreeIndex now indexes every entry (blob 100644/100755/120000, tree 040000, commit 160000), validates the fixed type/mode pairs and fails capture closed when a contents 404 matches any indexed entry; covered by github.spec.ts regression tests.

lowFollowups.issue: When capture fails at the capturing stage, the Policy budget already finalized is not released, so an agent can exhaust only its own rollback budget.
lowFollowups.exploitability: Self-denial of service; no integrity impact.
lowFollowups.recommendation: Release the budget reservation when discarding a capturing placeholder.
lowFollowups.evidence: Two-phase reserve (service.ts #reserveCompensation) holds capacity before capture and releases it on every pre-dispatch failure; crash recovery releases orphaned holds by idempotency key via assistant-policy releaseByIdempotencyKey. Pinned by compensation-service tests I/M/N/O/P and policy ledger/service tests.

lowFollowups.recommendation: Retain current conservative behavior; document it.

lowFollowups.note: Recorded fail-closed boundary; no code change.

secondPassReview.summary: A second independent four-dimension adversarial review (budget state machine, crash recovery, untrusted GitHub responses, auth/identity) ran over the followup working-tree diff. Three dimensions returned zero findings. The budget-state-machine dimension opened one medium: after the preimage seal but before the local dispatch flip, a failure released the budget hold while the old cleanup only discarded 'capturing' placeholders, leaving a live 'prepared' zombie that only the next process restart would terminalize. Source analysis narrowed the real trigger: the seal->flip span is fully synchronous and a signal abort cannot interleave there (it is intercepted while the row is still 'capturing'); the reachable window is the second #reserveCompensation recheck failing because the open reservation row was released by idempotency key through the assistant-policy API during the capture await. The fix adds ledger.abandonPreparedCompensation (a CAS prepared->unknown live counterpart of the recoverCompensations prepared branch, audited compensation-abandoned) and invokes it from the service catch for the never-dispatched prepared case, after the hold is released. unknown stays terminal and is never replayed, and the forward action's one compensation slot remains occupied exactly as crash recovery assigns.

verification.pass: adversarial verify of the original medium (workflow wf_21c7e5d2-c7a)
verification.detail: The verifier established the reviewer's signal-abort window is unreachable (service.ts:575 re-checks authorization and combined.aborted; the seal, prepared guard, second reserve recheck and dispatch flip are synchronous with no await), while independently confirming the working-tree fix closes the prepared-zombie harm: the catch calls abandonPreparedCompensation (CAS on status='prepared' AND expected version), returns undefined if dispatch won the race so a POSTed row is never downgraded, startup recoverCompensations plus releaseByIdempotencyKey handles hard-crash orphans, and same-key replay returns the terminal unknown without re-reserving or re-POSTing.

verification.pass: mutation test of regression test P
verification.detail: With the live prepared transition removed (call site replaced by a no-op), compensation-service test P fails with "expected 'prepared' to be 'unknown'"; restoring the fix makes it pass, proving the test cannot pass against the zombie behavior.

verification.pass: fresh independent adversarial re-audit of the final tree
verification.detail: A separate adversarial auditor re-read the complete compensation state machine in ledger.ts, #executeCompensation/#reserveCompensation/startup recovery in service.ts, the assistant-policy reserve/finalize/release/releaseByIdempotencyKey semantics and both tests, attempting to refute the fix. It confirmed: (1) the reachable trigger is exactly the capture-await window in which another connection releases the still-open reservation (stillAuthorized() at the post-capture recheck does not inspect policy holds, so the sealed prepared row reaches the second #reserveCompensation and fails there); signal abort / grant revoke / owner change cannot interleave in the synchronous seal->flip span and are correctly handled by the capturing branch. (2) abandon/dispatch cannot wrongly downgrade a POSTed row: both run in BEGIN IMMEDIATE with WHERE status='prepared' AND version=?; SQLite serializes the writers, and the service additionally gates on the in-memory dispatched flag. (3) Budget accounting is exactly-once: the external release already decremented reserved_amount and the catch release hits policy's idempotent released branch, so the period nets to zero with no double-release; a live row that was actually finalized is never released; live and restart recovery paths account identically. (4) unknown is terminal and never replayed: same-key replay returns the stored unknown before any reserve/POST; a different key against the same forward action hits UNIQUE(forward_action_id) conflict. (5) abandon's audit row is written in the same transaction as the CAS UPDATE; business errors still propagate. Residual observations (non-blocking): if abandon itself fails because the controller fence was lost, the row briefly stays prepared until restart recovery (no budget leak, fail-closed); #reserveCompensation maps all reservation errors to a coarse fail-closed denial; the trigger surface is the narrow policy-side concurrent-change window. Reverting the fix makes three independent assertions in test P red and the new ledger test fails on the missing primitive, so the tests genuinely pin the defect.

limitations: No real GitHub repository, account or token was authorized for this slice; local HTTP transport and integration evidence cannot establish live GitHub behavior or production permission correctness.
A compensation commit is visible append-only history and does not erase either the forward commit or itself.
A changed branch head blocks compensation rather than overwriting intervening work.
Unknown forward commits are ineligible because an exact succeeded forward receipt is required.
Unknown compensation dispatches stay occupied and are never automatically retried or relabeled from observed branch state.
Only the captured authorized files are restored; PR, CI, review/comment, message/notification, webhook, deployment, release and arbitrary external effects remain outside this protocol.
Private preimages contain repository file content and require the same private state-root ownership, retention and backup controls as the Actions ledger.

The independent adversarial review is complete (YES-WITH-FOLLOWUPS), a second four-dimension adversarial pass plus an adversarial recheck of the one medium it raised are complete, and the final root gate is re-run against the followup tree; LOW-1/LOW-2 were closed with code and tests, LOW-3/LOW-4 are retained as documented conservative boundaries, and the only open test gap is v2-to-v3 ledger migration coverage.
WP10 remains implementing and the complete 18-work-package objective remains active.
